facts.fact: At the e-justice conference of 17-18 September 2024 the panel with the Malawi Police Service's ICT officer reported that the service is working towards digitising its processes, including implementing a crime management system, and that digital records will reduce the need for paper-based documentation; UNDP's assessment presented there found most justice-sector processes still paper-based, the police's one named technology being a fingerprint system.

As reported at the conference of 17-18 September 2024, the Malawi Police Service is implementing a crime management system and has added to it a crime reporting feature through which victims report incidents for follow-up by the Crime Investigation Department; no station count or rollout date is given.

systems.tiers: not stated; being implemented as of September 2024

systems.system: crime reporting feature of the crime management system
systems.tiers: victims report incidents; followed up by the Crime Investigation Department

systems.country_label: Integrated Intelligence Electronic Case Management System (iCASE)
systems.platform: undecided: proprietary off-the-shelf (USD 2-4 million) or open-source, partly locally developed
systems.owner: justice-sector institutions led by the Judiciary, with UNDP support
systems.tiers: proposed across judiciary, police, prosecution, prisons and oversight bodies; not yet operational; annexed strategy costs it at USD 3,530,000 over 2023-2027

note: The crime management system is classed record on the statement that its digital records replace paper documentation; the document does not say that stations enter reports or cases in it, nor who funds it. The annexed e-justice strategy and its costing concern the justice-sector case management system, not the police system.
